data.title: Arab League Condemns Continued Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia
data.content:
Cairo, November 20, 2026, SPA -- The Arab League strongly condemned the Houthi terrorist militia's continued aggression against Saudi Arabia, including the latest attacks, which caused material damage to a tower in the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) in Riyadh.
    In a statement issued today, the Arab League said repeated attacks on civilian objects and vital facilities constitute a dangerous escalation, a flagrant violation of Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and a breach of international law. It warned that such attacks threaten the safety of citizens and residents in Saudi Arabia.
    The Arab League called for an immediate halt to the attacks, warning that they threaten regional security and stability and undermine efforts to de-escalate tensions and reach a political settlement to the Yemeni crisis.
    It reiterated its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for the measures the Kingdom takes to protect its security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, stressing that Saudi Arabia's security is an integral part of Arab national security.
    -- SPA
